input: Make a personalized family recipe book as a gift

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing who the recipient is (e.g., a parent, grandparent, sibling, whole family) shapes the tone, content selection, and personal touches included in the book.
The number of recipes and whose recipes are included determines the scale of the project — a small curated collection vs. a comprehensive multi-generational archive requires very different effort.
Whether the book is printed professionally, self-printed, or made digitally (e.g., PDF, photo book service) determines the tools, cost, and production steps involved.
The budget and deadline directly limit which format and production method are feasible and how much time can be spent gathering content.
The occasion (e.g., birthday, holiday, wedding) sets the urgency, the emotional register, and may influence thematic choices for the book.
The desired style and tone — rustic and handwritten-feeling vs. sleek and modern — determines layout, design choices, and whether to include photos, stories, or just recipes.
Understanding what 'done well' looks like — e.g., every recipe contributor feels represented, the recipient is moved emotionally, it is heirloom-quality — guides every prioritization decision.

gold.taskTitle: Create a Personalized Family Recipe Book Gift
gold.taskDescription: Compile and produce a personalized family recipe book to give as a meaningful gift to someone.

questions.title: Who is the intended recipient of this book?
questions.description: Identify the specific person or people this gift is for (e.g., a parent, grandparent, the whole family unit) to shape tone, content, and personal touches.

questions.title: How many recipes should the book include?
questions.description: Determine the scale — a small curated collection of favorites vs. a comprehensive multi-generational archive — to scope the content-gathering effort.

questions.title: What occasion or event is this gift for?
questions.description: Identify the gifting occasion (e.g., holiday, birthday, reunion, wedding) to set the deadline, urgency, and thematic direction.

questions.title: What is your budget for producing this book?
questions.description: Establish a spending limit to determine which production methods — professional printing service, self-printing, or digital-only — are realistic.

questions.title: Should the final book be physical, digital, or both?
questions.description: Decide on the output format (e.g., printed hardcover via a photo book service, a self-printed binder, a PDF) to determine the tools and production steps required.

questions.title: What visual style should the book have?
questions.description: Clarify the desired aesthetic — rustic and handwritten-feeling, clean and modern, vintage, illustrated — to guide layout, typography, and design decisions.

questions.title: Beyond recipes, what would make this feel truly special?
questions.description: Identify the emotional or qualitative bar for success — e.g., including family photos, handwritten contributor notes, personal stories, or heirloom-quality binding — to prioritize the right extras.
